answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 3 for each member already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival burns the most. The quill multiplier is published, charged in sparrow, and cipher lists each payment. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, as the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 549 identities would post 3151 proofs and burn roughly 83 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
